title: Courier Distances on a Weighted Tree
description:
A courier company serves n towns connected by n - 1 two-way roads; the roads form a tree (there is exactly one simple route between any two towns). Each road has a length. The company receives q delivery requests; request i asks for the length of the route between towns ai and bi.

To keep the output short, print the sum of the answers of all requests.

The tree can be very deep (think of a long chain), so walking up the tree for every request is too slow, and deep recursion will crash.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 6·104, 1 ≤ q ≤ 6·104
  • 1 ≤ length ≤ 106
  • ai = bi is allowed (distance 0).

Input

The first line contains n. Each of the next n - 1 lines contains u v w: a road of length w between towns u and v. The next line contains q, followed by q lines a b.

Output

Print one integer: the sum of the distances of all requests.

Example

Input:

5
1 2 3
1 3 5
3 4 2
3 5 7
3
2 4
4 5
1 1

Output:

19
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(d[0]); p = 1
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        u = int(d[p]); v = int(d[p + 1]); w = int(d[p + 2]); p += 3
        adj[u].append(v); adj[u].append(w)
        adj[v].append(u); adj[v].append(w)
    q = int(d[p]); p += 1
    qa = [0] * q; qb = [0] * q
    qs = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(q):
        a = int(d[p]); b = int(d[p + 1]); p += 2
        qa[i] = a; qb[i] = b
        qs[a].append(i)
        if b != a:
            qs[b].append(i)
    dep = [0] * (n + 1); par = [0] * (n + 1)
    f = list(range(n + 1)); vis = [False] * (n + 1)
    total = 0
    st = [1]
    while st:
        x = st.pop()
        if x < 0:
            f[-x] = par[-x]
            continue
        vis[x] = True
        for i in qs[x]:
            o = qa[i] + qb[i] - x
            if vis[o]:
                r = o
                while f[r] != r:
                    r = f[r]
                while f[o] != r:
                    f[o], o = r, f[o]
                total += dep[qa[i]] + dep[qb[i]] - 2 * dep[r]
        st.append(-x)
        a = adj[x]; px = par[x]
        for j in range(0, len(a), 2):
            y = a[j]
            if y != px:
                par[y] = x
                dep[y] = dep[x] + a[j + 1]
                st.append(y)
    print(total)
main()

title: Critical Junctions
description:
A road network has n junctions and m two-way roads. A junction is critical if closing it (together with all roads touching it) increases the number of connected pieces of the network. In other words, count the articulation points of the undirected graph.

To keep the output short, print the number of critical junctions and the sum of their labels.

Constraints

title: Rush Hour Route Count
description:
A city has n intersections and m two-way roads with positive travel times. Find the shortest travel time from intersection 1 to intersection n, and the number of different routes that achieve it. Two routes are different if their sequences of roads differ (so two parallel roads between the same intersections give different routes). The count can be enormous: print it modulo 109 + 7.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 105, 0 ≤ m ≤ 1.5·105
  • 1 ≤ time ≤ 109; distances may exceed 32-bit range.
  • Roads from an intersection to itself and repeated roads may appear.
  • If n = 1, the answer is 0 1 (the empty route).

Input

The first line contains n m. Each of the next m lines contains u v t.

Output

Print the shortest time and the number of shortest routes modulo 109+7, separated by a space; print -1 if intersection n is unreachable.

Example

Input:

4 5
1 2 1
1 3 1
2 4 1
3 4 1
1 4 3

Output:

2 2
solution:
import sys, heapq
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(d[0]); m = int(d[1])
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    p = 2
    for _ in range(m):
        u = int(d[p]); v = int(d[p + 1]); w = int(d[p + 2]); p += 3
        adj[u].append((v, w)); adj[v].append((u, w))
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    INF = float('inf')
    dist = [INF] * (n + 1); cnt = [0] * (n + 1); done = [False] * (n + 1)
    dist[1] = 0; cnt[1] = 1
    h = [(0, 1)]
    while h:
        du, u = heapq.heappop(h)
        if done[u]:
            continue
        done[u] = True
        cu = cnt[u]
        for v, w in adj[u]:
            nd = du + w
            dv = dist[v]
            if nd < dv:
                dist[v] = nd; cnt[v] = cu
                heapq.heappush(h, (nd, v))
            elif nd == dv:
                cnt[v] = (cnt[v] + cu) % MOD
    if dist[n] == INF:
        print(-1)
    else:
        print(dist[n], cnt[n])
main()

title: Wormhole Travel Times
description:
A galaxy has n stations and m one-way wormholes. Travelling through wormhole u v w takes w time units; w may be negative (you arrive before you left). Starting at station s at time 0, for every station determine the earliest possible arrival time. If you can travel around a negative cycle on the way to a station, its arrival time is unbounded below.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 400, 0 ≤ m ≤ 2500
  • -106 ≤ w ≤ 106
  • Self-loops and repeated wormholes are allowed. A negative self-loop is a negative cycle.

Input

The first line contains n m s. Each of the next m lines contains u v w.

Output

Print n lines; line v contains: INF if station v cannot be reached from s; -INF if its arrival time can be made arbitrarily small; otherwise the shortest arrival time. Station s itself has time 0 unless it is affected by a negative cycle.

6 7 1
1 2 4
2 3 -2
3 4 1
4 2 -1
3 5 3
1 5 10
6 1 1

Output:

0
-INF
-INF
-INF
-INF
INF

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 3000, 0 ≤ m ≤ 7000
  • 1 ≤ |a|, |b| ≤ n. A wish may repeat a literal (a = b, forcing it) or be a tautology (a = -b).

The first line contains n m. Each of the next m lines contains two non-zero integers a b.

1 2
-1 3
-2 -3
4 -3

title: Make the Network Fault-Tolerant
description:
A connected computer network has n nodes and m two-way cables. A cable is a weak link if cutting it disconnects the network. The engineers want to lay the minimum number of new cables (each new cable joins any two distinct nodes, possibly ones that are already joined) so that the resulting network has no weak link at all. title: Toll Vouchers
description:
A country has n cities and m two-way toll roads; road u v w costs w. You travel from city 1 to city n and own K vouchers. Using a voucher on a road makes that road free; each voucher can be used once, at most one voucher per road traversal. Find the minimum total toll.

Note that the best route with vouchers is generally not the cheapest route without them.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 6000, 0 ≤ m ≤ 2·104, 0 ≤ K ≤ 10
  • 1 ≤ w ≤ 109
  • Self-loops and repeated roads may appear. If n = 1 the answer is 0.

Input

The first line contains n m K. Each of the next m lines contains u v w.

Output

Print the minimum total toll, or -1 if city n cannot be reached.

Example

Input:

5 6 1
1 2 4
2 5 100
1 3 1
3 4 1
4 5 50
2 3 1

Output:

2
solution:
import sys, heapq
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(d[0]); m = int(d[1]); K = int(d[2])
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    p = 3
    for _ in range(m):
        u = int(d[p]) - 1; v = int(d[p + 1]) - 1; w = int(d[p + 2]); p += 3
        adj[u].append((v, w)); adj[v].append((u, w))
    K1 = K + 1
    INF = float('inf')
    dist = [INF] * (n * K1)
    dist[0] = 0
    h = [(0, 0)]
    pop = heapq.heappop; push = heapq.heappush
    while h:
        du, s = pop(h)
        if du > dist[s]:
            continue
        v, j = divmod(s, K1)
        if v == n - 1:
            print(du); return
        for y, w in adj[v]:
            b = y * K1 + j
            nd = du + w
            if nd < dist[b]:
                dist[b] = nd; push(h, (nd, b))
            if j < K:
                b += 1
                if du < dist[b]:
                    dist[b] = du; push(h, (du, b))
    print(-1)
main()
